[FreeSWITCH](https://signalwire.com/freeswitch) is an open-source softswitch.

- It answers calls and bridges them.
- It plays and records audio.
- It runs conferences and voicemail.

It works as a back-to-back user agent (B2BUA).

- A proxy such as OpenSIPS or Kamailio passes the caller's request on to the
  callee.
- A B2BUA instead answers the caller's call itself.
  - It places a second, separate call to the callee, with its own Call-ID.
  - It carries the audio of both calls through itself.

One call through FreeSWITCH is therefore two SIP dialogs, one per leg. Its
audio is four streams:

- caller to FreeSWITCH,
- FreeSWITCH to caller,
- the same pair on the callee's side.

This guide does the following:

- It builds FreeSWITCH from source.
- It sets it up to bridge a test call to a callee on the same machine.
- It proves it with a call that carries audio.

This guide does not use sipnab. When you have this working, [Run sipnab beside
FreeSWITCH](@/docs/freeswitch-sipnab.md) adds sipnab.

## Tested on

Every block on this page ran as written, in order, on 2026-10-12.

- The machines were clean x86_64 virtual machines with 2 cores and 3 GB of
  memory.
- They ran Debian 13 (kernel 6.12.63) and Ubuntu 24.04 (kernel 6.8.0).
- On each:
  - The build ran on a machine with nothing installed.
  - [Run sipnab beside FreeSWITCH](@/docs/freeswitch-sipnab.md) ran between the
    operate blocks in "Operate it" and the uninstall.
  - The uninstall ran last.
- Every test call carried audio both ways on both legs, counted on the wire.
- Causing each fault under [When something does not
  work](#when-something-does-not-work) produced the message it quotes, on both.

| Software | Version |
|---|---|
| FreeSWITCH | 1.11.3, the current release, built from the release archive on `files.freeswitch.org` |
| sofia-sip (FreeSWITCH's SIP stack) | 1.13.18, built from the `v1.13.18` tag of `github.com/freeswitch/sofia-sip` |
| spandsp (FreeSWITCH's signal-processing library) | 3.1.1, built from the `v3.1.1` tag of `github.com/freeswitch/spandsp` |
| SIPp (for the test call) | the distribution's `sip-tester`: 3.7.3 on Debian 13, 3.7.2 on Ubuntu 24.04 |

The examples use `192.0.2.10` as the machine's address. Replace it with yours
everywhere it appears.

## Install FreeSWITCH

### What each distribution offers

FreeSWITCH's own packages come from SignalWire's package repository. That
repository answers only with a SignalWire account's access token.

- Neither distribution carries a `freeswitch` package.
- The versions of sofia-sip and spandsp they carry are older than FreeSWITCH
  1.11.3 accepts. It needs:
  - sofia-sip 1.13.18 or later,
  - spandsp 3.1.1 or later.

This block shows all three on your machine:

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y ca-certificates curl
apt-cache policy freeswitch libsofia-sip-ua-dev libspandsp-dev
. /etc/os-release
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' "https://freeswitch.signalwire.com/repo/deb/debian-release/dists/$VERSION_CODENAME/Release"
```

- `apt-cache policy` prints nothing for `freeswitch`.
- It prints a `Candidate` of:
  - 1.12.11 for `libsofia-sip-ua-dev`,
  - 0.0.6 for `libspandsp-dev`.
- The last line prints `401`. That is the HTTP status for a request that needs
  credentials.

| | Debian 13 | Ubuntu 24.04 |
|---|---|---|
| A `freeswitch` package from the distribution | none | none |
| SignalWire's FreeSWITCH packages | need a SignalWire access token | need a SignalWire access token |
| Build from source, as below | no account needed | no account needed |

This guide builds from source.

- That needs no account.
- The same steps work on both distributions.
- The build installs everything under `/usr/local/freeswitch`.
  - sofia-sip and spandsp are the exception. They go under `/usr/local`.

### Build sofia-sip and spandsp

First the compiler, the build tools, and the libraries FreeSWITCH's core and
its default modules use:

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git build-essential automake autoconf libtool libtool-bin pkg-config xz-utils \
  libssl-dev zlib1g-dev libjpeg-dev libtiff-dev libsqlite3-dev libcurl4-openssl-dev libpcre2-dev \
  libspeex-dev libspeexdsp-dev libldns-dev libedit-dev uuid-dev libopus-dev libsndfile1-dev liblua5.4-dev yasm nasm
```

Then the two libraries. They come from the FreeSWITCH project's own
repositories, at the versions FreeSWITCH 1.11.3 asks for:

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/src/voice && sudo chown "$USER": /usr/local/src/voice
cd /usr/local/src/voice
git -c advice.detachedHead=false clone --depth 1 -b v1.13.18 https://github.com/freeswitch/sofia-sip.git
git -c advice.detachedHead=false clone --depth 1 -b v3.1.1 https://github.com/freeswitch/spandsp.git
for d in sofia-sip spandsp; do (cd "$d" && ./bootstrap.sh && ./configure && make -j2 && sudo make install); done
sudo ldconfig
pkg-config --modversion sofia-sip-ua spandsp
```

The last line prints `1.13.18` and `3.1.1`.

### Build FreeSWITCH

`modules.conf` lists the modules the build compiles. Four of the default ones
need libraries this guide does not install:

- `mod_signalwire` and `mod_verto` need SignalWire's `libks`.
- `mod_av` needs the FFmpeg development libraries.
- `mod_pgsql` needs the PostgreSQL client library.

The `sed` line leaves those four out:

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
cd /usr/local/src/voice
curl -fsSLO https://files.freeswitch.org/releases/freeswitch/freeswitch-1.11.3.-release.tar.xz
curl -fsSL https://files.freeswitch.org/releases/freeswitch/freeswitch-1.11.3.-release.tar.xz.sha256 | sha256sum -c -
tar xf freeswitch-1.11.3.-release.tar.xz
cd freeswitch-1.11.3.-release
sed -i -E 's#^(applications/mod_av|applications/mod_signalwire|endpoints/mod_verto|databases/mod_pgsql)$#\#\1#' modules.conf
./configure
make -j2
sudo make install
sudo ln -sf /usr/local/freeswitch/bin/freeswitch /usr/local/freeswitch/bin/fs_cli /usr/local/bin/
freeswitch -version
```

- `sha256sum -c` prints `freeswitch-1.11.3.-release.tar.xz: OK`.
  - The checksum comes from the same server as the archive.
  - So it detects a damaged download, not a changed one.
- The last line prints `FreeSWITCH version:
  1.11.3-release~64bit (-release 64bit)`.

The release archive's name has a dot before `-release`. That is the name on the
server.

### Run it as a service

FreeSWITCH runs as its own user.

- This unit is the one in the FreeSWITCH source tree,
  `debian/freeswitch-systemd.freeswitch.service`, with the paths of this
  build.
- FreeSWITCH starts as root.
  - It raises its own scheduling priority.
  - Then it drops to the `freeswitch` user.
- `-ncwait` makes `systemctl start` wait until FreeSWITCH is ready to take
  commands:

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
sudo useradd --system --home-dir /usr/local/freeswitch --shell /usr/sbin/nologin freeswitch
sudo chown -R freeswitch:freeswitch /usr/local/freeswitch
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/freeswitch.service >/dev/null <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=FreeSWITCH
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=forking
PIDFile=/usr/local/freeswitch/run/freeswitch.pid
ExecStart=/usr/local/freeswitch/bin/freeswitch -u freeswitch -g freeswitch -ncwait -nonat
TimeoutSec=45s
Restart=always
LimitCORE=infinity
LimitNOFILE=100000
LimitNPROC=60000
LimitSTACK=250000
LimitRTPRIO=infinity
LimitRTTIME=infinity
IOSchedulingClass=realtime
IOSchedulingPriority=2
CPUSchedulingPolicy=rr
CPUSchedulingPriority=89
UMask=0007

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable freeswitch
```

`-nonat` stops FreeSWITCH from asking the local router to forward ports to it
(UPnP and NAT-PMP).

## Configure FreeSWITCH

`make install` put FreeSWITCH's example configuration in
`/usr/local/freeswitch/conf`. The FreeSWITCH project calls it "vanilla". It
runs two SIP profiles. Each profile is a SIP listener with its own settings:

- `internal`, on port 5060, for your own phones.
  - It asks every caller for a user name and password.
- `external`, on port 5080, for carriers and other servers.
  - It asks for no password.
  - It sends each call to the dialplan's `public` context.

The test call in "Place a test call" goes to `external`.
This block changes five things:

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
cd /usr/local/freeswitch/conf
sudo sed -i 's|=stun:stun.freeswitch.org"|=192.0.2.10"|' vars.xml
P=$(od -An -tx1 -N12 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')
sudo sed -i "s|data=\"default_password=1234\"|data=\"default_password=$P\"|" vars.xml
sudo sed -i 's|<param name="listen-ip" value="::"/>|<param name="listen-ip" value="127.0.0.1"/>|' autoload_configs/event_socket.conf.xml
sudo sed -i -E 's#^( *)(<load module="mod_(verto|signalwire|av)"/>)#\1<!-- \2 -->#' autoload_configs/modules.conf.xml
sudo tee dialplan/public/01_echo.xml >/dev/null <<'EOF'
<include>
  <!-- A call to "echo" goes to the test callee on this machine, in PCMU. -->
  <extension name="test_callee">
    <condition field="destination_number" expression="^echo$">
      <action application="bridge" data="{absolute_codec_string=PCMU}sofia/external/echo@127.0.0.1:5070"/>
    </condition>
  </extension>
</include>
EOF
sudo chown -R freeswitch:freeswitch /usr/local/freeswitch/conf
grep 'stun-set' vars.xml
sudo systemctl restart freeswitch
fs_cli -x 'sofia status'
```

What the changes do:

- **The machine's address.**
  - `external_rtp_ip` and `external_sip_ip` are the addresses FreeSWITCH puts
    in its SIP and SDP for the `external` profile.
  - The example configuration asks the public STUN server
    `stun.freeswitch.org` for them at startup.
  - That gives the address of your internet connection, not of this machine.
  - With that default, the `Contact` header of FreeSWITCH's replies to the
    test call named the public address.
  - On a machine with its own public address, put that address here.
- **The SIP password.**
  - `default_password` is the password of the 20 example users, `1000` to
    `1019`, that the `internal` profile accepts.
  - The example configuration sets it to `1234`.
  - The block replaces it with a random one.
- **The event socket.**
  - `fs_cli` is FreeSWITCH's command-line client.
  - It talks to FreeSWITCH over its event socket, TCP port 8021, with the
    password `ClueCon`.
  - The example configuration listens on every address.
  - The block moves it to `127.0.0.1`, so only this machine reaches it.
- **Modules the build left out.**
  - The example configuration loads `mod_verto`, `mod_signalwire` and
    `mod_av`.
  - The section "Install FreeSWITCH" did not build them.
  - Without this line, FreeSWITCH logs `Error Loading module` for each at
    every start.
- **Where the test call goes.**
  - The dialplan is FreeSWITCH's routing.
  - FreeSWITCH bridges a call to `echo` in the `public` context to a test
    callee on this machine, `127.0.0.1:5070`.
  - `absolute_codec_string=PCMU` makes FreeSWITCH offer the callee PCMU only.
    That is the one codec SIPp's callee answers with.

`sofia status` lists the profiles. Both are `RUNNING`:

- `internal` shows `sip:mod_sofia@192.0.2.10:5060`.
- `external` shows `sip:mod_sofia@192.0.2.10:5080`.

## Place a test call

SIPp plays both ends:

- a callee on this machine that echoes audio back,
- a caller that calls `echo` on FreeSWITCH's `external` profile and plays a
  recorded G.711 sample.

So the call carries real audio both ways. The caller uses port 5090, because
FreeSWITCH holds 5060 and 5080:

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
sudo apt-get install -y sip-tester jq
mkdir -p ~/sipp/pcap && cd ~/sipp
ln -sf /usr/share/sip-tester/*.pcap pcap/
sipp -sn uas -i 127.0.0.1 -p 5070 -rtp_echo -m 1 -bg
sudo sipp -sn uac_pcap 192.0.2.10:5080 -i 192.0.2.10 -p 5090 -s echo -m 1 -timeout 90s
```

- The caller needs `sudo` because it plays the audio sample through a raw
  socket.
- It sends about 7 seconds of audio, then a short DTMF clip, and hangs up.
- At the end SIPp's statistics screen shows `Successful call` at 1.

SIPp's built-in caller sends its `ACK` and `BYE` straight to FreeSWITCH.
FreeSWITCH is the far end of the caller's dialog. Unlike the proxy guides,
this guide needs no edited scenario.

Each leg has its own audio.

- The caller offers PCMA, and FreeSWITCH answers it in PCMA.
- On the callee's leg FreeSWITCH offers PCMU.
- FreeSWITCH converts the audio between the two codecs.

[Run sipnab beside
FreeSWITCH](@/docs/freeswitch-sipnab.md) shows all four streams.

## Operate it

**See a call's two legs while it is up.** FreeSWITCH calls each leg a
channel. Start a call in the background and list the channels:

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
cd ~/sipp
sipp -sn uas -i 127.0.0.1 -p 5070 -rtp_echo -m 1 -bg
sudo sipp -sn uac_pcap 192.0.2.10:5080 -i 192.0.2.10 -p 5090 -s echo -m 1 -timeout 90s -bg
sleep 3
fs_cli -x 'show channels as json' | jq -r '.rows[] | "\(.direction) \(.name) \(.read_codec)"'
sleep 12
```

```text
inbound sofia/external/sipp@192.0.2.10:5090 PCMA
outbound sofia/external/echo@127.0.0.1:5070 PCMU
```

- The `inbound` channel is the caller's leg, in PCMA.
- The `outbound` one is the callee's, in PCMU.
- The last line waits for the call to end.

**Check health and read the logs.**

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
systemctl is-active freeswitch
fs_cli -x status
sudo tail -n 30 /usr/local/freeswitch/log/freeswitch.log
```

- `fs_cli -x status` prints:
  - FreeSWITCH's version,
  - its uptime,
  - the number of sessions since it started.
- FreeSWITCH writes its log to `/usr/local/freeswitch/log/freeswitch.log`, not
  to the journal.

**Apply a configuration change.**

- A change to the dialplan or the users takes effect with `reloadxml`.
- A change to `vars.xml` or a SIP profile needs a restart:

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
fs_cli -x reloadxml
sudo systemctl restart freeswitch
fs_cli -x status | head -2
```

`reloadxml` prints `+OK [Success]`.

**Uninstall.** Remove FreeSWITCH, its user, and the two libraries:

```bash
# Run all of these, in order.
sudo systemctl disable --now freeswitch
sudo rm -rf /usr/local/freeswitch /etc/systemd/system/freeswitch.service /usr/local/bin/freeswitch /usr/local/bin/fs_cli
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo userdel freeswitch
sudo make -C /usr/local/src/voice/sofia-sip uninstall
sudo make -C /usr/local/src/voice/spandsp uninstall
sudo rm -rf /usr/local/include/sofia-sip-1.13 /usr/local/include/spandsp /usr/local/share/sofia-sip
sudo ldconfig
rm -rf /usr/local/src/voice/sofia-sip /usr/local/src/voice/spandsp /usr/local/src/voice/freeswitch-1.11.3.-release*
```

## When something does not work

- **The test call fails, and SIPp reports `Aborting call on unexpected message
  ... received 'SIP/2.0 488 Not Acceptable Here`.**
  - The callee answered with a codec FreeSWITCH had not offered it.
  - Without `absolute_codec_string`, FreeSWITCH offers the callee the caller's
    codec, PCMA.
  - SIPp's callee answers PCMU whatever FreeSWITCH offers.
  - FreeSWITCH's log shows `Originate
    Failed.  Cause: INCOMPATIBLE_DESTINATION`.
  - Keep `{absolute_codec_string=PCMU}` in the `bridge` line, or offer your
    callee a codec it supports.
- **`fs_cli` prints `[ERROR] fs_cli.c:1699 main() Error Connecting []`.**
  - Nothing answers on the event socket. One of these is true:
    - FreeSWITCH is not running.
    - Its `listen-ip` is not the address `fs_cli` connects to, `127.0.0.1`.
  - Check `systemctl status freeswitch`.
